subject: gunblade

Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Lionheart Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a chrome revolve-chamber below, a long blued blade above, trimmed in gold with a crimson lion emblem and glowing runes.
spec.layout: A trophy pose: the gunblade stands vertical, dead centred on x = 0, pommel resting on the floor and the blade tip up at y = 2.2. From the bottom up: a wrapped grip with a flared pommel and a hanging tassel (y 0 to 0.55), a gold trigger guard looped forward with a curved trigger inside (y 0.15 to 0.5, forward of +Z), then the gun mechanism (y 0.5 to 1.0): a six-shot revolver drum with its axle along Y, a barrel housing rising into the blade root, a cocked hammer at the back (−Z), and a side plate carrying the crimson lion emblem. A gold crossguard flare crowns the mechanism (y 0.9 to 1.05), and from it the long blade rises to a pointed tip (y 1.05 to 2.2). The blade's wide flat face looks toward +Z and its width runs along X, so the front view shows the full silhouette: dark steel with a bright polished fuller down the centre, a gold edge inlay, and five glowing amber runes marching up the flat. Everything reads as heavy sculpted metal: faceted low-poly forms, gold fittings at every joint between parts, dark ink seams, crimson accents only on the emblem and grip knot. Rests on the floor only at the pommel base and the trigger guard's lowest curve.

parts.builds: The handle assembly from pommel to the top of the grip. A flared faceted pommel cap (steel, 6-8 sided frustum) sitting exactly on y = 0 at pommelBase, with a gold ring under it and a small gold lion-face stud on each flank. The grip itself: a slightly tapering frustumBox column in gripLeather, wrapped with four evenly spaced raised gripWrap bands and one gold wire band near the top; a crimson cord knot with two short hanging tails (crimson rods, tips in gold) ties off below the guard. The trigger guard: a gold arc swept from the grip front down and forward to a round gold front post at z ≈ +0.14, flat in the XZ plane, thick enough to read as forged (a swept tube with faceted section); inside it hangs the trigger, a curved crimson-steel hook on the trigger joint, with an ink-dark inner face. A small gold ring at the guard's rear top where it meets gripTop.
parts.attaches: Pommel base sits on the floor at pommelBase; the grip's top face meets mechanism at gripTop (y 0.55); the trigger guard's rear ring bolts to gripTop's lower rim.

parts.builds: The gun heart of the weapon, from gripTop to bladeRoot. The revolver drum: a 6-sided faceted cylinder, axis along Y centred on cylinderAxis, radius 0.13, height 0.2, in steelDark with a steel top and bottom cap plate; each of its six flanks carries one recessed chamber: a small steelDark-to-steelInk cylinder stub, and one chamber bears a live brass-gold round head peeking out (gold disc). Gold band rings clamp the drum top and bottom. Behind the drum at the back (−Z), the hammer: a steel forging swept up and back from the mechanism body, a faceted cocked spur with a crimson inlay stripe, riding the hammer joint so it reads as spring-loaded. The barrel housing: a rectangular steel block rising from barrelRoot toward bladeRoot, flanked by two steelInk side plates with three silver hex screw heads each, and a small gold plate on the right flank. The front (facing +Z) carries a barrel muzzle ring (gold) around a dark steelInk bore that continues up into the blade root, and a tiny bone sight bead on top. The lion emblem: a crimson shield-shaped plate (extrude, about 0.16 wide and 0.2 tall) seated proud on the front-right flank of the housing, with a gold stylized lion head built from a few bold extruded blades: a ring mane, a muzzle, two ears and two gold eyes, all seated on the plate, plus ink outline pieces so the emblem reads from two meters.
parts.attaches: Bottom sits on gripTop (y 0.55) centred on cylinderAxis; the hammer hinges at the back of the housing; the top face (barrelRoot to bladeRoot) is covered by the guard part; the drum centre spins on the cylinder joint.

parts.builds: The crossguard and blade root collar, the gold crown of the piece. A swept-back flared guard: two mirrored gold extruded wings (smoothing 2, bevelled, about 0.22 long each) sweeping from the blade root down and back over the drum shoulders like a comb, sharp at their tips, plus one straight gold bar across the front just above the muzzle ring. Where the guard meets the blade at guardTop, a gold collar ring (short faceted lathe) grips the blade root, with a row of eight small steelInk studs studded around it via a ring, and one crimson gem (small octahedron, gold bezel) set at the front centre of the collar. Under the collar, three short steel cooling fins (thin extruded blades) step down the barrel housing so the transition from gun to sword is layered, not abrupt.
parts.attaches: Sits over mechanism's top: the wings land on the drum shoulders at y 0.86-0.9, the collar clamps the blade at guardTop (y 1.05), gem and front bar sit forward toward +Z.

parts.builds: The great blade from guardTop to the tip at y 2.2. One long extruded silhouette in steel, drawn in the XY plane (width along X, thickness along Z about 0.035): root width 0.11 swelling to 0.14 at the mid-blade, then a long taper to a sharp point, with a subtle gunblade recurve on the cutting edge (+X side: gentle S through the length) and a straighter back edge. A raised steelInk fuller rail: a second thin extruded strip seated proud down the centre flat, in steelDark, from collar to the last quarter. The cutting edge wears a silver inlay: a slim silver extruded strip seated along the +X edge face for the whole length. The back (−X) edge carries a short row of three gold serration wedges near the mid-blade. A gold ricasso band crosses the blade just above the collar, and a pierced steelDark rectangle cutout (a small extruded frame) sits mid-blade as a balance hole. The tip's last 0.2 m is capped in silver. Flat shading throughout so the facets read as ground and honed steel.
parts.attaches: Blade root enters the guard's collar at guardTop (y 1.05), riding the bladeJ joint up from bladeRoot.

parts.builds: The magic and finishing details that live on the blade and hilt. Five glowing amber runes (runeGlow, emissive): small extruded angular glyphs, each a different simple mark (chevron, triangle, cross, bar pair, diamond), seated proud on the blade's +Z flat face in a vertical march from y 1.25 to 2.0, each with a thin steelInk outline plate slightly larger behind it so the glow is rimmed. The runes' glow is doubled at the blade root where a faint amber glow seam (a thin glowing strip) runs around the collar, as if the chamber feeds the blade. On the pommel, a hanging tassel upgrade: three bone-coloured cords with crimson tips dangle from the gold pommel ring, each a thin swept rod with a small gold cap bead. A single silver inlaid streak runs diagonally across the mid-blade fuller rail as a battle scar.
parts.attaches: Runes and scar seat on the blade's front flat (blade part); the glow seam wraps the guard collar at guardTop; the tassel hangs from grip's pommel ring at pommelBase.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec for a gunblade (Final Fantasy VIII style) — a large sword with a revolver-like mechanism. Static weapon, floor: true (it can rest on floor or be displayed). Let me plan.

Gunblade: iconic blade (like Squall's, though Squall's has no trigger... actually FF gunblades: blade with a revolver chamber near the hilt, trigger on grip). Best to spec an upright display stance, resting on floor, blade pointing up (+Z front? Model faces +Z — the weapon should face +Z). Perhaps the gunblade standing upright, tip up, or held horizontally resting. Standing vertically is readable: grip low, blade up. But box layout: blade along +Z facing forward? A weapon "faces +Z" — lay it horizontal, hilt at back, blade tip forward at +Z, resting on the floor or a small stand? Floor contact: blade edge touches floor. Better: display leaning/standing vertically, hilt at bottom. Then "front" +Z is the side profile. Hmm.

Simplest for builders: gunblade standing upright like planted in the ground, hilt bottom, barrel-blade up, plus maybe slightly angled. Height ~2.2m (FFVIII gunblades are big, ~1.5m). Let's do a 2.1 m tall standing weapon: grip and trigger guard at bottom (0–0.55), revolver chamber and cylinder block (0.55–0.95), long blade up to 2.1. Width ~0.45, depth ~0.5.

Parts (3–6):
1. gripAssembly — handle, trigger guard, trigger, pommel, grip wrappings/rings. floor: true.
2. mechanism — the revolver cylinder, chamber barrel, side plates, screws, hammer, firing pin detail, gauge. sits on grip.
3. blade — the long blade (metal), fuller, edge, tip.
4. trimOrnaments — lion emblem, red accent decals, blade root collar, crossguard flare, studs, chain? Maybe separate into "guardAndEmblem" and "energyRunes/glow".

Add glow: FF8 gunblade doesn't glow much but a Limit Break flash — could add glowing runes/edge accents. Style kit toon? Final Fantasy style: chrome steel, gold trim, red accents, lion emblem (Sleeping Lionheart). Palette: steel, dark steel, gold, crimson, bone/grip brown, glow amber.

Joints: could keep static (joints: []) — but trigger and hammer could be hinge joints. Maybe include a few joints: "hilt" root, "hammer" hinge, "trigger" hinge, "cylinder" hinge (rotates). Give it some rig. Spec joints created before parts: root "hilt" at grip, plus hammer, trigger, cylinderRevolve.

Budgets: sum ≤ 900. e.g. 180+200+200+170+120 = 870.

Mounts: gripTop where grip meets mechanism, cylinderAxis, bladeRoot where mechanism meets blade, guardTop.

Size: width x 0.5, height y 2.2, depth z 0.55.

Layout description front to back: front (+Z) is the blade's face (the wide flat side seen), etc. If standing upright, the blade is a vertical extruded shape, thickness along x, width along z? Gunblade blades are wide in one plane. Standing upright: blade flat plane facing ±X or facing ±Z. Model "faces +Z" — put the wide face toward +Z: blade flat plane in XY, thickness along Z? Wait, that makes the profile viewed from front show blade width. Hmm, blade width along z then. Actually the blade of a gunblade runs along its length; seen from the front (+Z) you'd see the wide face if the width axis is x. Let's think: sword lying vertically, wide face normal pointing forward +Z means the width runs along x (left-right). Front view shows the full blade silhouette: good. So blade cross-section: width along x (~0.12), thickness along z (~0.03), length along y.

Trigger guard etc. similar plane.

Mounts coordinates: centerline x=0. Grip occupies y 0–0.55. Blade root at y ~0.95.

Parts:
1. grip (id "grip"): pommel at y 0–0.12, grip 0.12–0.55, trigger guard, trigger, grip rings, floor: true. box y 0–0.6.
2. mechanism ("mechanism"): revolver chamber: cylinder (axis along... the barrel axis is the blade direction = +Y here). Cylinder drum with axis along y, radius ~0.13, at y 0.55–0.75; barrel housing 0.75–0.95; hammer at back; side plates; screws. box y 0.5–1.0.
3. blade ("blade"): y 0.9–2.2. Fuller, edge trim, tip.
4. guard ("guard"): crossguard/bullet-shaped flare at blade root y 0.85–1.0, gold trim, red emblem plate, studs — plus a small stand? No — the weapon stands alone? A sword can't stand on grip alone... fine, stylistically planted. Maybe lean: give a slight tilt? Keep vertical; pommel rests on floor. Fine.
5. ornaments ("runes"): glowing runes down the blade, engraved lion emblem on mechanism plate, chain tassel hanging from pommel? Tassel hanging — nice detail. Budget 120.

Joints: root "hilt" at [0, 0.3, 0] role hinge? Root joint role... use "spine"? Roles: spine neck head jaw hinge tail leg arm wing digit tentacle fan. For a weapon: hammer = hinge, trigger = hinge, cylinder = hinge (revolve). Root "hilt" role "spine". Parts ride joints.

Spec JSON. Keep it thorough but compact.
